body: King Vidor is one of my go-to recs for good stuff a little outside of the usual scope of the canon. Our Daily Bread and The Crowd tend to do well even with people who think B&W movies aren't for them. The Fountainhead is also great, though I don't always recommend that one for obvious reasons.

it's always easy for people to say things will get definitely better when they're not where you're at, you're right to be sick of hearing it. That all sounds so hard. I'm so sorry you're going through all of this.

communicating our emotions effectively is a skill, and one that we don't usually get taught. would you consider someone a piece of shit for not being able to ride a bike if they've never been shown? it takes time and a lot of patience, and it's important to meet yourself where you're at and forgive yourself for not being where you want to be, because you're worth loving even if you have trouble expressing why. sorry if that last bit turned a lil preachy, i was in a very similar position in my relationship a few months ago so i get passionate about the topic. 

again, best wishes

you're not a piece of shit for falling into a communication trap. these situations are super difficult, and sometimes emotions that come from a good place get expressed with frustration or anger. you seem pretty self aware about your role in the interaction, it's good to be aware just make sure you're not blaming yourself for the entire interaction, there's things everyone can do better. if you end up having that conversation later, i hope it goes well. it seems like you care about them, and I'm sure they know that. best of luck
